items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Now, then you had Bricktops, she had her cabaret and you had the Cubans, they were there.

ctx.x: So you be playing those flatted Fifths and all that stuff, he said we can do that better. (unintelligible) so you just go ahead and play what is you, so so far as his drumming the people liked it, and he worked all the time.

Now, then you had Bricktops, she had her cabaret and you had the Cubans, they were there. Everybody was there. I lived in a hotel called Hotel Rocheschour; it was on Boulevard . Now, Cubans was doing it -- after Afro Cubans stuff and you better be careful, because they'll get you, because you had to play your stuff and play well -- in a big casino, they have a Cuban playing the tipic music and you play jazz, and he'd leave it awful warm out there for you.
When you started putting yourself on there, it started raining and he's happy. Wasn't no sense in moving nothing but jealousy. It was each man doing his stuff and doing it well.
